```{r libraries, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(PKNCA)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

Yu and colleagues compared mechanism-informed machine-learning models (a gated
recurrent unit network and XGBoost) against a Bayesian population
pharmacokinetic (PopPK) model for forecasting tacrolimus trough concentrations
in the first 7 days after kidney transplantation. The machine-learning models
predict a per-patient composite exposure parameter and elimination rate from
the patient's history; they have no fixed parametric form and are not
population PK models, so they are not distributed here.

The PopPK comparator is a population model in its own right, and it is the one
distributed as `Yu_2026_tacrolimus`. It keeps the two-compartment structure of
the Francke 2025 model (`modellib("Francke_2025_tacrolimus")`), with every
absorption and disposition parameter fixed to the Francke estimates, and
re-estimates only the apparent oral clearance CL/F on the Michigan cohort. The
genotype covariates of the parent model were removed because genotype was
unavailable, and a new CL/F covariate model (race, body weight, age and
haematocrit) was built by stepwise selection (Supplementary Table S2). The
parameter estimates are in Supplementary Table S3.

* Citation: Yu H, Qin Z, Smith LS, Park JM, Zhu H-J. Mechanism-informed
  machine learning for individualized tacrolimus dose adjustment in the early
  post-kidney transplant period. *Br J Clin Pharmacol*. 2026;92(6):1730-1743.
  [doi:10.1002/bcp.70448](https://doi.org/10.1002/bcp.70448)

# Population

The model was fitted to 4311 whole-blood trough concentrations (LC-MS/MS,
LLOQ 1.0 ng/mL) from 1624 adult kidney transplant recipients treated at the
University of Michigan Hospital between 2001 and 2025 (Table 1). Mean age was
51.9 years (SD 13.8), 37.3% were female, 66.1% Caucasian, 23.7% African
American and 10.2% Other. Mean weight was 87.4 kg (SD 21.1) and mean
haematocrit 27.9% (SD 4.3). All recipients took twice-daily oral
immediate-release tacrolimus, started within 24 h of transplantation at
0.075 mg/kg every 12 h and then adjusted by trough-guided therapeutic drug
monitoring; the administered daily dose averaged 11.8 mg/day (SD 3.6) and the
observed trough 9.7 ng/mL (SD 4.0). Most patients (60.3%) contributed only two
troughs in the 7-day window (Supplementary Figure S2).

```{r population}
mod <- readModelDb("Yu_2026_tacrolimus")
str(mod()$meta$population, give.attr = FALSE, max.level = 1)
```

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 2-compartment, first-order absorption, lag time | -- | Methods, Population pharmacokinetic modelling (Francke 2025 structure) |
| `ltlag` | 0.375 h (held at the Francke 2025 value) | Supplementary Table S3, Tlag_pop |
| `lka` | 6.59 1/h (held at the Francke 2025 value) | Supplementary Table S3, ka_pop |
| `lcl` | 24.3 L/h | Supplementary Table S3, CL_pop |
| `lvc` | 705 L (held at the Francke 2025 value) | Supplementary Table S3, V1_pop |
| `lq` | 8.54 L/h (held at the Francke 2025 value) | Supplementary Table S3, Q_pop |
| `lvp` | 7670 L (held at the Francke 2025 value) | Supplementary Table S3, V2_pop |
| `e_age_cl` | -0.307 | Supplementary Table S3, Age (years) |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.692 | Supplementary Table S3, Weight (kg) |
| `e_race_black_cl` | 0.401 | Supplementary Table S3, Race (AA) |
| `e_hct_cl` | -0.394 | Supplementary Table S3, Hematocrit (%) |
| `etalcl` | 0.514^2 = 0.2642 | Supplementary Table S3, omega_CL (SD; CV 54.9%) |
| `propSd` | 0.281 | Supplementary Table S3, b (proportional error) |
| Covariate centring: 87.4 kg, 51.9 years, 27.9% | -- | Table 1 study-cohort means (not printed for the model; see Assumptions) |
| CL/F = CL_pop x exp(0.401 x AA) x (WT/87.4)^0.692 x (AGE/51.9)^-0.307 x (HCT/27.9)^-0.394 x exp(eta) | -- | Monolix covariate model on the log-normal CL/F; Supplementary Tables S2-S3 |
| Proportional residual error | -- | Methods, Population pharmacokinetic modelling |

The printed CV of 54.9% for omega_CL matches `sqrt(exp(0.514^2) - 1)`,
which confirms that 0.514 is the SD of a log-normal random effect (the exact
value is 54.99%, so Monolix's 54.9 is truncated rather than rounded; reading
0.514 as a variance would give a CV of 82%):

```{r omega-check}
omega_sd <- 0.514
cv_pct <- 100 * sqrt(exp(omega_sd^2) - 1)
round(cv_pct, 2)
stopifnot(abs(cv_pct - 54.9) < 0.15)
```

# Virtual cohort

200 virtual recipients with covariates drawn to match the Table 1 means and
SDs, truncated to plausible adult ranges. Race is drawn as African American
with probability 0.237 (Table 1).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  AGE = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 51.9, 13.8), 18), 80),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 87.4, 21.1), 45), 160),
  HCT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 27.9, 4.3), 18), 42),
  RACE_BLACK = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.237)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    race = ifelse(RACE_BLACK == 1, "African American", "Caucasian or Other"),
    # Michigan starting dose: 0.075 mg/kg every 12 h, rounded to 0.5 mg.
    dose = round(0.075 * WT * 2) / 2
  )

cohort |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Age (years)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(AGE), sd(AGE)),
    `Weight (kg)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(WT), sd(WT)),
    `Haematocrit (%)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(HCT), sd(HCT)),
    `African American (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(RACE_BLACK)),
    `Dose per 12 h (mg)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(dose), sd(dose))
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Virtual cohort, mean (SD).")
```

# Simulation

Each recipient receives the Michigan starting regimen for 7 days (14 doses at
0, 12, ..., 156 h). The simulation holds the starting dose constant; the real
cohort's doses were adjusted by therapeutic drug monitoring after the first
troughs, so the later simulated troughs show where the starting dose alone
would have taken each patient. Observations are on the `central` state; the
model returns `Cc` at each of them.

```{r simulate}
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 168, by = 1), seq(0, 12, by = 0.25), seq(144, 156, by = 0.25))))

dose_rows <- cohort |>
  dplyr::select(id, dose) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 156, by = 12)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, time, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")

obs_rows <- cohort |>
  dplyr::select(id) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(obs_rows, dose_rows) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort, id, AGE, WT, HCT, RACE_BLACK), by = "id") |>
  # Observation before dose at a shared time, so a pre-dose row is a trough.
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, evid)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, returnType = "data.frame", keep = "RACE_BLACK") |>
  dplyr::mutate(race = ifelse(RACE_BLACK == 1, "African American", "Caucasian or Other"))
```

## Typical-value profile

The reference recipient (87.4 kg, 51.9 years, haematocrit 27.9%, not African
American) receiving 6.5 mg every 12 h.

```{r typical}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
ev_typ <- rxode2::et(amt = 6.5, ii = 12, addl = 13, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 168, by = 0.25), cmt = "central")
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ, ev_typ,
  params = c(WT = 87.4, AGE = 51.9, HCT = 27.9, RACE_BLACK = 0),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)

ggplot(typ, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(8, 12), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 168, 24)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Tacrolimus whole-blood concentration (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Dashed lines: the 8-12 ng/mL target range used in Yu 2026."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The fixed 7670 L peripheral volume with Q/F = 8.54 L/h gives a peripheral
filling time of the order of `V2/Q` = 900 h, so trough concentrations are
still rising at the end of the first week under a constant dose.

# Replicate published figures

## Trough concentrations over the first week

Supplementary Figure S3 shows the observed troughs against time since the
first dose; they scatter between about 2 and 25 ng/mL with a regression line
near 10 ng/mL throughout the week. The simulated troughs (with residual error
added) under the constant starting dose are shown below with the observed
mean +/- SD of Table 1 (9.7 +/- 4.0 ng/mL) as a band.

```{r troughs-figure}
troughs <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% seq(12, 168, by = 12)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, sim, race)

trough_summary <- troughs |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(trough_summary, aes(time)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 9.7 - 4.0, ymax = 9.7 + 4.0, alpha = 0.15, fill = "darkorange") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 9.7, colour = "darkorange", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.3, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_point(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 168, 24)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Trough concentration (ng/mL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Blue: simulated median and 90% interval (constant starting dose, residual error included).",
      "Orange: observed mean +/- SD of all troughs (Table 1).",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Most observed troughs fall between 24 and 72 h (Supplementary Table S1: 2942
of 4311). Restricting the simulated troughs to that window:

```{r trough-check}
early <- troughs |> dplyr::filter(time >= 24, time <= 72)
early_summary <- early |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Mean (ng/mL)` = mean(sim), `SD (ng/mL)` = sd(sim), `Median (ng/mL)` = median(sim),
    `In 8-12 ng/mL (%)` = 100 * mean(sim >= 8 & sim <= 12)
  )
knitr::kable(early_summary, digits = 1, caption = "Simulated troughs at 24-72 h under the starting dose.")

stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed CL/F, a unit error or a wrong centring
  # value of the order of the cohort spread moves the whole distribution
  # far outside this window around the observed 9.7 ng/mL.
  abs(median(early$sim) / 9.7 - 1) < 0.3
)
```

The simulated median in the 24-72 h window is close to the observed mean
trough. The comparison is approximate, not exact: the observed doses were
adjusted by therapeutic drug monitoring (mean 11.8 mg/day, against about
13 mg/day for the starting dose in this cohort), and the observed troughs
pool all times in the first week.

## Covariate effects on CL/F

Typical CL/F across the covariate ranges of the cohort, each covariate varied
alone with the others at the reference values. The model's own `cl` output is
checked against the closed-form covariate equation.

```{r covariate-effects}
grid <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(covariate = "Weight (kg)", value = seq(50, 140, by = 10), WT = value, AGE = 51.9, HCT = 27.9, RACE_BLACK = 0),
  tibble::tibble(covariate = "Age (years)", value = seq(20, 80, by = 10), WT = 87.4, AGE = value, HCT = 27.9, RACE_BLACK = 0),
  tibble::tibble(covariate = "Haematocrit (%)", value = seq(18, 42, by = 4), WT = 87.4, AGE = 51.9, HCT = value, RACE_BLACK = 0),
  tibble::tibble(covariate = "African American", value = c(0, 1), WT = 87.4, AGE = 51.9, HCT = 27.9, RACE_BLACK = value)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())

ev_grid <- grid |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", WT, AGE, HCT, RACE_BLACK)
# Each id is a covariate setting, solved at the typical value; rxode2 warns
# that a multi-subject solve has no omega, which is intended here.
cl_grid <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_grid, returnType = "data.frame"),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  }
) |>
  dplyr::select(id, cl) |>
  dplyr::left_join(grid, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cl_closed = 24.3 * exp(0.401 * RACE_BLACK) * (WT / 87.4)^0.692 * (AGE / 51.9)^-0.307 * (HCT / 27.9)^-0.394
  )

# Same parameters on both sides: the difference is pure arithmetic.
stopifnot(all(abs(cl_grid$cl / cl_grid$cl_closed - 1) < 1e-8))

ggplot(cl_grid, aes(value, cl)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue4") +
  facet_wrap(~covariate, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Typical CL/F (L/h)") +
  theme_bw()
```

African American recipients have a typical CL/F of
`r round(24.3 * exp(0.401), 1)` L/h, `r round(exp(0.401), 2)`-fold that of
the reference recipient.

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental analysis of the first (0-12 h) and the last (144-156 h)
dosing interval of the simulation, by race group. Both intervals start with a
pre-dose observation (the first at time zero), so no defensive time-zero row
is needed. The predicted concentration `Cc` (no residual error) is used. The
day-1 Cmin is the zero concentration before the first dose; the day-7 Cmin is
the trough. The lower day-7 exposure of African American recipients reflects
their 1.49-fold higher CL/F at the same weight-based dose.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, race)

dose_df <- dose_rows |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort, id, race), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, race)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | race + id, concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | race + id, doseu = "mg")

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 144), end = c(12, 156),
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)

res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(res$result)

nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::group_by(race, start, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::mutate(interval = ifelse(start == 0, "Day 1 (0-12 h)", "Day 7 (144-156 h)")) |>
  dplyr::select(race, interval, cmax, tmax, cmin, auclast) |>
  dplyr::arrange(interval, race) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Race" = race,
    "Interval" = interval,
    "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "Cmin (ng/mL)" = cmin,
    "AUC0-12 (ng*h/mL)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median NCA parameters under the constant starting dose.")
```

# Comparison against published values

Yu 2026 reports no non-compartmental parameters, so there is no published NCA
table to compare against. The available published quantities are the observed
trough summary (Table 1), compared in the trough section above, and the
internal model-selection results (Supplementary Table S2), which cannot be
reproduced without the patient data. The paper's predictive-performance
metrics for this model (Table 2: internal MSE 9.27 ng^2/mL^2, R^2 0.450;
external MSE 8.96 ng^2/mL^2, R^2 0.211) come from sequential Bayesian
forecasting on individual patient histories and likewise need the patient
data.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate centring values.** Supplementary Table S3 prints the four
  covariate coefficients but not the reference values the continuous
  covariates were centred on. The coefficients are those of log-transformed
  covariates on the log-normal CL/F (a linear-per-kg reading would make the
  weight effect `exp(0.692 x 20)` per 20 kg, which is impossible), and Monolix
  centres a transformed covariate on a cohort summary value. The maintainers
  used the study-cohort means of Table 1: 87.4 kg, 51.9 years and 27.9%. If the
  authors centred on the medians instead, the typical CL/F at a given
  covariate set would differ by a few percent; the comparison with the
  observed troughs above does not resolve that difference.
* **Race reference group.** Race was recorded as Caucasian, African American
  or Other, but Table S3 prints only an African American coefficient. The
  Other group is therefore pooled with Caucasian as the reference
  (`RACE_BLACK = 0`).
* **Haematocrit over time.** The Methods describe haematocrit as a
  time-varying laboratory value matched to each dose and trough. The paper
  does not say whether the Monolix fit used it time-varying or per patient;
  the model accepts either.
* **Parameters held at the Francke 2025 values.** Lag time, ka, V1/F, Q/F and
  V2/F were not estimated in this analysis; they are encoded with `fixed()`.
  They match the Francke 2025 Table 2 estimates distributed in
  `Francke_2025_tacrolimus`.
* **Machine-learning models not included.** The GRU and XGBoost models
  estimate a per-patient composite parameter `alpha` (about F/Vd) and an
  elimination rate from each patient's history (Equation 2) and have no
  population parameters to distribute.
* **Virtual cohort.** Covariates are drawn independently from normal
  distributions with the Table 1 means and SDs; the paper does not give
  covariate correlations or ranges.
